title: 🎙️ Qwen Audio 3.1 speaks 65 languages.. a huge voice update from Alibaba!
body: 🎙️ Qwen Audio 3.1 speaks 65 languages.. a huge voice update from Alibaba!
Alibaba's Qwen team has announced a wide update to the Qwen Audio 3.1 voice models, expanding language support across its three services without changing the architecture or prices.

Speech-to-text now covers 59 languages and 8 Chinese dialects, after covering only 30 languages before, while text-to-speech now covers 65 languages and 6 dialects, and real-time voice chat now covers 53 languages and 6 dialects.

The models rely on a mixture-of-experts architecture trained on about 20 million hours of multilingual audio, through stages including pretraining, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, and are offered as cloud services through APIs without downloadable weights.

The series first appeared on 23 September at the Apsara conference, with five models covering recognition, synthesis and real-time chat, with price cuts reaching 95% on some services, and the new update only expands the languages on the three production services.

The technical documentation noted a striking paradox: despite the number of languages nearly doubling, the documented number of Chinese dialects fell from 16 to 8, with no explanation from the company of how this number is measured.
Simply put: an AI that hears you and talks with you in 65 languages, and the Chinese dialects alone fill a list; are many languages enough to make a voice assistant truly global?
Do you talk to a voice assistant in your language, or do you still prefer typing?
